message.content:
Use `maxsplit` to stop after the first “=”:

```python
temp = "hello=good="
parts = temp.split('=', 1)   # ['hello', 'good=']
print(parts)
```

If you called `temp.split('=')` without the second argument, you’d get `['hello', 'good', '']` because it splits on *every* “=”. By passing `1`, you tell Python to perform at most one split, so the remainder of the string (including any remaining “=”) stays together.
